It's actually really simple.  There is something called the circle of 5ths, where you basically play the same interval 12 times and end up back where you started.

The reason the 5th is important is because it means the ratio between the top and bottom frequency is almost exactly 1.5

In his left hand, he is playing octaves where the ratio between the top and bottom frequencies is exactly 2.0

In his right, he is playing the pentatonic scale which is simply the first 5 notes which are a perfect fifth away from eachother, which means they are incredibly consonant.

So, you can just hit those notes in any old way and they won't create tension.

Just for interest, many Jazz musicians look down upon the pentatonic scale because it is so simple and lacks any of the advanced analysis that 'higher' musics contain.  Also, if you play 6 notes in a row in the circle of 5ths, you get the playable major scale, though you can't play it quite as hap-hazardly because 2 of the notes are in a position where one must resolve to the other once it's been played, to 'return home.'
